angle: On the factory floor, AI value shows up as OEE, scrap, and uptime—not slideware.
linkedinPost:
Industrial AI’s ROI isn’t a model—it’s a factory.

McKinsey’s view on US manufacturing is clear: winning will take capital, talent, energy, and resilient suppliers. From the floor, I’d add: AI that actually ships into OT and moves OEE, scrap, and uptime.

Pilots are easy in a lab. Plants are noisy, unionized, safety-first, and allergic to downtime. That’s the point: value lives there.

What works:
- Start with line-centric use cases: vision for quality, predictive maintenance, scheduling—not moonshots.
- Co-design with operators and maintenance. If they won’t use it on a night shift, you built a demo.
- Integrate with MES/SCADA and honor change-control. “Shadow IT” dies at the gate.
- Measure like ops: OEE, scrap rate, mean time between failures. Celebrate fewer stoppages, not more dashboards.
- Commit to uptime SLAs for your AI service, same as any critical equipment vendor.

If your AI program can’t survive a safety audit or a shutdown drill, it won’t scale in manufacturing.

What single metric would convince your plant manager that AI is paying rent? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #CustomerExperience
